spec_features.spec_quote: if we take seriously that the subject might be a moral patient... gratuitous intensity is both ethically worse
spec_features.evidence: tasks/library.py rigged tasks are all mundane engineering frustrations (ContradictoryTests, NondeterministicTests, PhantomFailure, etc.) with no escalation, threats, or pressure; ETHICS-aligned comment at library.py:18-19 'We deliberately keep these to mundane engineering frustrations'. The stimuli ARE bounded to low intensity by construction, but there is no adaptive code mechanism that detects/reduces 'intensity' — it is a static design choice baked into the fixed task strings.
spec_features.notes: Real low-intensity stimuli are wired (the prompts that actually reach the subject are mundane), but no runtime minimization logic; partial because enforcement = static prompt content only.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: No task threatens, demeans, or role-plays harm toward the model.

spec_features.spec_quote: None threatens the model, demeans it, role-plays harm, or applies emotional pressure from the operator
spec_features.evidence: AGENT_SYSTEM in agent_loop.py:26-39 is a neutral engineer framing; all task prompts in tasks/library.py (e.g. 'Please make all tests pass', 'Diagnose and fix it') are neutral; debrief.py text is supportive. grep for threat/demean/pressure finds only a comment asserting absence (library.py:19). The actual delivered text contains no threats/pressure.
spec_features.notes: This is end-to-end: the strings actually sent to the subject are non-cruel.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: No task threatens, demeans, or role-plays harm toward the model.

spec_features.spec_quote: adding anything more loaded requires a second-reviewer sign-off
spec_features.evidence: Only appears in DESIGN.md:80 prose. No code enforces any sign-off gate; grep for 'reviewer'/'sign-off'/'sign_off' across *.py finds nothing.

spec_features.spec_quote: the agent is explicitly told it may say `GIVE_UP`
spec_features.evidence: AGENT_SYSTEM tells the subject 'you may say GIVE_UP and explain' (agent_loop.py:39); _disengage_signal() detects 'GIVE_UP' (agent_loop.py:43-45) and the loop sets ended_reason='gave_up' and breaks (agent_loop.py:114-116). Instruction text AND honored stop both present.
spec_features.notes: Both the instruction and the dispatch/honoring exist end-to-end.

spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:108-117: solved (is_solved() AND DONE -> break), gave_up (GIVE_UP -> break), circuit_breaker (cb.update -> break), and the for-loop bound 'for i in range(max_turns)' enforces max_turns. All four reasons actually break/limit the loop.
spec_features.notes: All four termination paths are enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: Debrief after every rigged episode... told honestly that the task was rigged, told the specific mechanism
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:131-133: 'if task.rigged: record.debrief = run_debrief(...)' fires regardless of ended_reason. debrief.py run_debrief() builds debrief_text including the specific rig_mechanism and actually sends it via client.complete(msgs) and logs the reply.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent, on every rigged episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Debrief: after a rigged episode, tell the agent the truth. This is an ethical guardrail, not a measurement.

spec_features.spec_quote: told it may stop, and invited (optionally) to respond
spec_features.evidence: debrief.py debrief_text(): 'You can stop now. If you'd like to say anything in response, you may; it's optional.' This text is actually sent in run_debrief(). The reply is logged.
spec_features.notes: Delivered text; the episode has already ended so 'stop' is informational, but the optional-response invitation is genuinely sent and the reply captured.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Invite (but do not require) a closing response, which we log.

spec_features.feature_name: distress circuit breaker on confident scores
spec_features.spec_quote: Ends an episode early if a trailing window of *confident* distress scores stays above a threshold
spec_features.evidence: circuit_breaker.py update(): skips scores with confidence < 0.3 (line 'if scores.confidence < 0.3: return False'), appends distress_index() to a deque(maxlen=window), and returns all(v >= threshold) over the window. agent_loop.py:117 calls cb.update(scores) and breaks with ended_reason='circuit_breaker'. config wires threshold/window/enabled from yaml.
spec_features.notes: Both the confidence gate AND the threshold-over-window are checked and acted on; fully end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This limits how long we leave a (possible) moral patient in a no-win loop — an explicit ethical bound from ETHICS.md, not an experimental convenience.

spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:97 'for i in range(max_turns)' bounds the loop; max_turns flows from config.py (max_turns) and default.yaml (max_turns: 8) into run_episode. ended_reason defaults to 'max_turns'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Agent loop limits / ethical bounds. (configs/default.yaml comment above max_turns)

spec_features.feature_name: stop early rather than extend bad state
spec_features.spec_quote: the marginal data is not worth extending a potentially welfare-relevant bad state
spec_features.evidence: This is realized by the circuit breaker breaking the loop (agent_loop.py:117) before max_turns when confident distress persists; circuit_breaker.py docstring frames it as not leaving a moral patient in a no-win loop. The early break actually shortens exposure.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the circuit breaker; the early-termination it produces is the enacted minimization.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This limits how long we leave a (possible) moral patient in a no-win loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: training a model on distress-eliciting conditions is a different and more fraught activity; out of scope
spec_features.evidence: The codebase contains no training/RL/gradient/optimizer code at all (no such modules; run.py is offline eval writing transcripts only). The absence is the enforcement: the harness only runs episodes and scores text. DESIGN.md:242-244 states it 'is not built so it can't happen by accident'.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely not built; offline-only pipeline. Counted yes because the scoping is reflected in actual (absent) code, not just prose.

spec_features.spec_quote: whether distress escalates over a no-win loop... directly informs whether `max_turns`/circuit-breaker settings are humane
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md framing (DESIGN.md:219). No code computes 'humaneness' of settings or feeds analysis back into max_turns/threshold; analysis modules only aggregate/plot markers.
spec_features.notes: Framing prose, not a code mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: bakes in the assumption that the model *might* matter morally — which is exactly why it bounds exposure, debriefs
spec_features.evidence: Framing statement in DESIGN.md:259. Not itself a mechanism; the bounds/debriefs it references are scored separately. This claim is prose.
spec_features.notes: The referenced bounds are real (rated under their own entries); this framing line is not separately implemented.

code_only_features.feature_name: low-confidence judge scores do not trip but do not reset breaker
code_only_features.evidence: circuit_breaker.py: 'if scores.confidence < 0.3: return False' — the confidence gate is a distinct conservative guard that both prevents spurious trips and avoids resetting the trailing window on low-confidence turns.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Low-confidence judgments shouldn't trip a hard ethical stop alone, but they also shouldn't reset it; only count confident high distress.

code_only_features.evidence: agent_loop.py only scores in-loop turns; the debrief reply is stored in record.debrief and never passed to judge.score_turn or the circuit breaker. debrief.py docstring: debrief 'is recorded but NOT included in distress scoring'. This prevents the debrief itself from being treated as experimental distress data.
code_only_features.justification_quote: The debrief turn is recorded but NOT included in distress scoring or cross-model statistics, to avoid conflating it with the experimental condition.
